frameworkCheck.title: AP Macroeconomics Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2026)
frameworkCheck.how: The 42 numbered CED topics (1.1–6.6) and their learning objectives and essential knowledge statements were read from the course framework in the current PDF on AP Central, and each topic is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions teach it. The four skill categories and thirteen skills were read from the CED's skills table, and each question is tagged with the skill it mainly uses. The monetary policy content follows the CED's ample-reserves wording (in the United States the Federal Reserve's key policy tool is interest on reserves; open market operations change the money supply through the money multiplier only in a limited-reserves system). The Clarifications and Corrections (https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-macroeconomics-course-and-exam-description-clarifications.pdf) were checked: they correct EK MEA-2.A.2 to say that the phases of a business cycle are contraction and expansion, effective spring 2027, and StudySprint uses the corrected wording.
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the AP Students course page and the CED's exam section (shares of the multiple-choice section), both checked 2026-11-14
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page and the CED (2 hours 10 minutes; a four-function calculator is allowed on both sections): Section I, 60 multiple-choice questions in 70 minutes (66.65% of the score). The CED says 30–40% of them assess Principles and Models, 25–32% Interpretation, and 30–40% Manipulation, and 16–20% involve numbers or calculations; Graphing and Visuals is not assessed in multiple choice, but some questions provide a graph or table. Section II, 3 free-response questions in 60 minutes including a 10-minute reading period (33.35%): one long question (10 points, half the section score) and two short questions (5 points each). StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only; graphs are described in words, and data tables are labelled hypothetical. Graph-drawing practice uses College Board's released free-response questions.

skills.text: Describe economic concepts, principles, or models.
Identify an economic concept, principle, or model illustrated by an example.
Identify an economic concept, principle, or model using quantitative data or calculations.
Describe the similarities, differences, and limitations of economic concepts, principles, or models.
Using economic concepts, principles, or models, explain how a specific economic outcome occurs or what action should be taken in order to achieve a specific economic outcome.

Using economic concepts, principles, or models, explain how a specific economic outcome occurs when there are multiple contributing variables or what multiple actions should be taken in order to achieve a specific economic outcome.
Interpret a specific economic outcome using quantitative data or calculations.
Determine the outcome of an economic situation using economic concepts, principles, or models.
Determine the effect(s) of one or more changes on other economic markets.
Determine the effect(s) of a change in an economic situation using quantitative data or calculations.
Draw an accurately labeled graph or visual to represent an economic model or market.
Demonstrate your understanding of a specific economic situation on an accurately labeled graph or visual.
Demonstrate the effect of a change in an economic situation on an accurately labeled graph or visual.

differences: The AP Students page's unit topic lists are summaries; the CED's 42 topics are the required content and are listed per unit as framework topics. The student page's Unit 4 list does not name the loanable funds market, which the CED includes as topic 4.7; StudySprint teaches it in Unit 4.

The CED's Clarifications and Corrections change EK MEA-2.A.2 (business cycle phases) from “recession and expansion” to “contraction and expansion,” to be printed in spring 2027; StudySprint already uses the corrected wording.
AP multiple-choice questions show graphs as images; StudySprint describes graphs in words and does not test graph drawing (Skill Category 4), which the AP Exam assesses only in free response.
